names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 10 mai, «Sfântul Mucenic Alfeu».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 10 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Αλφειός, Κυπρίνος και Φιλάδελφος οι Αυτάδελφοι Μάρτυρες», with the rank word left off; the page's own head line for him is «Αγιος Αλφειος ο Μαρτυρας».

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 10 May, „Свети мученици Алфеј, Филаделф и Кирин.“ — Свети left off, which is not a rank, and мученици left off, which is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types`. One rank word stands over all three names and belongs to none of them; the heading gives no epithet, no city and no year, and the brotherhood, the father, southern Italy, Sicily and Licinius are all in the body. A direct walk of every `names` entry in `saints/` finds no folder holding Алфеј, so the form folds with nothing.

The heading of the calendar’s name link, «Алфий Бастийский, Месопольский, мч.», with the rank abbreviation left off and the forename taken with the first epithet only, as `acacius-the-centurion` took his in batch ru-05-07-1. The day’s own line declines him «Мчч. Алфия» among four others. `fk.mjs` returned NONE before the write.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 10 мая ст. ст. — «Мчч. Алфия , Филадельфа , Киприана , Онисима , Еразма и иных (251).»

attestations.note: The identification is exact: one line of the Russian calendar names the same five men this corpus already keeps on the menologion’s 10/5, with the same year, 251, and the calendar carries a separate name link for each. `dates` is unchanged — the folder’s 249–251 from saint.gr contains the Russian 251. The life the five share, life1031, is a company of nineteen and names only these five; «и иных» on the day line and «и 14 других» in the life’s own title are fourteen men the source does not name, so they are not folders and are named as a refusal in the report. The life sets the persecution under «император Ликиний» and then dates the brothers’ passion to 251 «при императоре Декии» — two reigns sixty years apart in one paragraph, which is the source’s own disagreement and is recorded and not resolved; the folder keeps the Decian date it already had. The Russian name link gives him two epithets the day line does not, «Алфий Бастийский, Месопольский», and the life accounts for both: he was sent from Rome to Mesopolis in the territory of Leontini in Sicily. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 10 mai — «Sfântul Mucenic Alfeu»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Αλφειός, Κυπρίνος και Φιλάδελφος οι Αυτάδελφοι Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and gives each of the three brothers his own head line and his own distich. **`dates` are added where the folder had none**, as the reign the page prints and nothing narrower. **The Greek adds what the folder lacked**: that the three were brothers, sons of the ruler of the prefects Vitalius, from the country of the Vascones of southern Italy; that they were taught the Orthodox faith and baptised by a venerable man named Onesimus; that they were denounced, seized by one Anengelion under Decius and sent bound to Rome; that after the first examination they were taken on to Puteoli to the governor Diomedes, who sent them to Tertyllus the ruler of Sicily; and that Tertyllus, failing to change their minds, condemned them to death. **His own death is the page's**: they cut out his tongue and then beheaded him. **`related` rows are added for the other two brothers and for the two martyrs of the same day**, `erasmus-10-may` and `onesimus-10-may`, whose own page says they died «μαζί με τους Άγιους Μάρτυρες Αλφειό, Κυπρίνο και Φιλάδελφο». **The venerable Onesimus who baptised them is not identified with the martyr Onesimus of the same day**: the Greek gives the one Ὅσιος and the other Ἅγιος Μάρτυρας and joins them nowhere, and that question is left in the report. No relics, no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 23.05.2026 (10. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Алфеј, Филаделф и Кирин.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, an enumerated company of three, so one row each, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek both keep them on. **THE REIGN IS A DIFFERENT EMPEROR AND THE DATE WAS NOT TOUCHED.** This book kills the three „у време цара Ликинија“, in the time of the emperor Licinius, where saint.gr has them seized by Anengelion „επί αυτοκράτορα Δεκίου (249-251 μ.Χ.)“ — Decius against Licinius, sixty years and two reigns apart. The folder's `death` 249–251 is saint.gr's reading of Decius's reign; **the Prologue gives Licinius with no bounds at all**, and the coordinator's standing refusal of a reign with no bounds means it cannot be turned into an interval or used to widen one. So `dates` are unchanged and the disagreement is recorded here and in the life. **A SECOND DISAGREEMENT, about his own death**: this book has his tongue cut off and „Од излива крви Алфеј умре“, he died of the flow of blood, where saint.gr has them cut out his tongue **and then behead him**. Both stand in the life. **New here**: that the three were brothers born of one womb, sons of a certain prince Vitalis in southern Italy, „Дивни у благородству, силни у вери“, judged for their faith and led from one judge to another and from one torturer to another, taken over into Sicily and killed there; **that their incorrupt relics were found in 1517**, which is a date for the relics and not for the man, so it is in the life and not in `dates`; and **that the three brothers appeared to Saint Euthalia**, with the book's own cross-reference „(в. 2. март)“. **`related_add: ["euthalia-the-martyr"]` is the row that appearance owes**, and the reciprocal is in the same upgrade file: her own life, written off the Prologue's Julian 2 March and off the Romanian and Greek pages, already tells the dream of these three, and her folder carried no `related` key at all. **The father Vitalis takes nothing.** This book calls him „некога кнеза Виталија“, a certain prince, and the Greek „ο άρχων των επάρχων“; the corpus's four Vitalis folders were read and he is none of them — a venerable of 11 January, a martyr at Ravenna in 62, a Sicilian monk of 994, and the Alexandrian who is the author's own open pair with `vitalis`. No folder anywhere, so by the coordinator's third ruling the row has nothing to attach to and no folder is minted. **No `locations`**: southern Italy and Sicily are places this folder has never claimed as points. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr gives a reign and no year: «συνελήφθηκαν από τον Ανηγγελίωνα επί αυτοκράτορα Δεκίου (249-251 μ.Χ.)». The interval is that reign as the page prints it.
